translation: Pallavi (Chorus): Let's go, let's go to the fair, oh mother... let's bring jasmine and malle flowers, let's go to the fair; let's go, let's go to the fair, oh mother... let's bring jasmine and malle flowers, let's go to the fair; the whole village has risen as one... all the people of our hamlet are on the move (Let's go, let's go to the fair, oh mother... let's bring jasmine and malle flowers, let's go to the fair) (The whole village has risen as one... all the people of our hamlet are on the move)

Verse 1: Wearing new clothes, to the fair... let's play the kolatam stick-dance, to the fair; all the young folk together, to the fair... let's dance the chindu steps, let's go to the fair; wearing new clothes, to the fair... let's play the kolatam stick-dance, to the fair; all the young folk together, to the fair... let's dance the chindu steps, let's go to the fair (Let's go, let's go to the fair, oh mother... let's bring jasmine and malle flowers, let's go to the fair)

Verse 2: Let's hitch up the bullock cart, to the fair... together with all our relatives, to the fair; at the goddess's temple, to the fair... let's fulfil our vows, to the fair; let's hitch up the bullock cart, to the fair... together with all our relatives, to the fair; at the goddess's temple, to the fair... let's fulfil our vows, to the fair (Let's go, let's go to the fair, oh mother... let's bring jasmine and malle flowers, let's go to the fair)

Verse 3: With the beat of the dappu drums, to the fair... let's dance with swaying heads, to the fair; with the blessings of our village mother, to the fair... let's live in flourishing joy, to the fair; with the beat of the dappu drums, to the fair... let's dance with swaying heads, to the fair; with the blessings of our village mother, to the fair... let's live in flourishing joy, to the fair
(Let's go, let's go to the fair, oh mother... let's bring jasmine and malle flowers, let's go to the fair) (The whole village has risen as one... all the people of our hamlet are on the move)
summaryEn: Categorised as a Festival song, this piece captures the collective excitement of villagers setting off together to a jatara, the seasonal temple fair central to Telangana folk religious life. The refrain word 'jatharo', repeated after nearly every phrase, works like a rhythmic exclamation binding the whole song to the idea of the fair itself. The pallavi describes the whole village - 'ooru vaada' - moving as one body toward the festival, carrying jasmine and malle flowers as offerings. The verses build a vivid picture of festival preparation and participation: putting on new clothes, young people playing the kolatam stick-dance and chindu folk dance, families hitching bullock carts and travelling together with relatives, visiting the goddess's temple to fulfil vows (mokkulu), and finally dancing to dappu drums in a trance-like sway, seeking the blessing of the 'palle thalli' (village mother goddess) for a prosperous, green life. The song has no named individual speaker; it is a communal invitation, sung in first person plural throughout, evoking the shared anticipation and social bonding of a village jatara procession.
summaryTe: పండుగల కోవకు చెందిన ఈ పాట తెలంగాణ జానపద జీవితంలో ముఖ్యమైన జాతర సందర్భంగా గ్రామస్థులంతా కలిసి బయలుదేరే సందడిని చిత్రిస్తుంది. దాదాపు ప్రతి పదబంధం తర్వాత వచ్చే 'జాతరో' అనే పల్లవి పదం పాట మొత్తాన్ని జాతర భావనతో ముడిపెడుతుంది. పల్లవిలో ఊరు వాడ అంతా ఒక్కటై, జాజి మల్లెలు తీసుకుని జాతరకు కదిలిపోవడం కనిపిస్తుంది. చరణాల్లో కొత్త బట్టలు వేసుకోవడం, యువకులు కోలాటం, చిందులు వేయడం, బండ్లు కట్టుకుని బంధువులతో కలిసి ప్రయాణించడం, అమ్మవారి గుడి వద్ద మొక్కులు చెల్లించడం, డప్పు దరువులకు శిగమూగుతూ ఆడటం వంటి జాతర సన్నాహాలు, వేడుకలు వర్ణించబడ్డాయి. చివరగా పల్లె తల్లి దీవెనలతో అంతా పచ్చగా, సుభిక్షంగా ఉండాలని కోరుకుంటారు. పాట మొత్తం 'మనం' అనే భావనతో సాగుతూ, గ్రామ జాతర ఊరేగింపులో ప్రజలు పంచుకునే ఆనందాన్ని, ఐక్యతను ప్రతిబింబిస్తుంది.
